description: Wire fixtures for the media contract: the server drives them through HTTP, the clients through their fake gateway, so a drift between the two is caught here rather than when the parts are first put together. Change them only together with libs/protocol/media.ts and libs/domain/media.ts. One rule runs through all of them — the bytes never pass through the API: the browser writes them by signature and reads them from storage or a CDN, and no fixture here carries a file body.

fixtures.name: upload-grant-put
fixtures.description: A grant where the provider has no POST policy — every Bunny zone. Size and type are bound by signing their headers, which is the only way to bind them on a presigned PUT.

fixtures.name: upload-grant-post
fixtures.description: The same call where a POST policy exists (AWS, MinIO): the range is a policy condition. Also the shape of a file above the hashing limit, which carries no checksum and is not deduplicated.

fixtures.name: upload-complete
fixtures.description: The record as storage describes it — size and type from the HEAD, not from the client — and the durable `/media/<id>` path a block stores.

fixtures.name: media-page
fixtures.description: One page of the library, in the shape the admin's gallery already expects. Only `ready` files appear, and never another school's.

fixtures.name: resolve-urls
fixtures.description: A screen's worth of playable addresses in one call, with the expiry rounded to the window boundary so the address is shared and cacheable. An unreadable id is absent, not null.

fixtures.name: storage-profile
fixtures.description: Credentials in, never out: the answer carries the key id and four characters of the secret. `delivery` is derived from the presence of a CDN host, and applying the call retires the old profile instead of editing it.

fixtures.name: refusals
fixtures.description: Every refusal with its status and message key, including where it happens: the quota is refused at the grant, not at completion.
